segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he showed me a river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing out from the throne of God and of the Lamb

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: down the middle of the city’s main street. On either side of the river was the tree of life, bearing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit each month; and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No longer will there be anything under a curse. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city, and his slaves will serve him;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there will be no more night. They have no need of the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, because the Lord God will shine on them, and they will reign forever and ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “These words are faithful and true. The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent his angel to show his slaves what must happen soon.”

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “And look, I am coming soon! Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I had heard and seen them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who was showing them to me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Don’t do that! I am a fellow slave with you and your brothers the prophets and those who keep the words of this book. Worship God!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: Let the one who does wrong still do wrong, and the filthy still be filthy, and the righteous still do righteousness, and the holy still be holy.”

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, I am coming soon, and my reward is with me, to repay each one according to their work.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify to you about these things for the assemblies. I am the root and the descendant of David, the bright morning star.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Spirit and the bride say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Come!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And let the one who hears say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Come!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who wishes take the water of life as a gift.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to that person the plagues written in this book;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away that person’s share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are written about in this book.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The one who testifies to these things says,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Yes, I am coming soon.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.

notes.phrase: down the middle of the city’s main street
notes.traditional: In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life
notes.note: The Greek can be punctuated two ways. Read with verse 1, as here and in the edition translated, the river flows down the middle of the street. Read with what follows, as in the King James Version, the tree of life stands in the middle of the street as well as beside the river. The Greek says ‘its street’, meaning the city described in chapter 21.

The image recalls the tree of life in the garden of Genesis 2–3, from which humanity was barred, and Ezekiel 47:12, where trees line both banks of a river flowing from the temple. The Greek noun is singular although it stands on both sides of the river; it may be meant collectively, as a kind of tree.

The Greek says simply ‘twelve fruits’. Many translations take this as twelve varieties; the following clause, ‘yielding its fruit each month’, suggests twelve harvests a year, which is the reading adopted here. Either is possible.
This is the same Greek word that this translation renders ‘Gentiles’ where the non-Jewish peoples are meant. In Revelation the scope is the peoples of the whole world, so ‘nations’ is used.

The word is rare and can mean either a curse or a thing placed under one. The sentence echoes Zechariah 14:11, where the underlying idea is the ban that devoted a city to destruction. The promise is that nothing in the new Jerusalem will ever again fall under it.

The word meant a slave, someone owned by a master, and a first-century reader would have heard it that way. Most English versions soften it to ‘servants’, partly because the Septuagint uses it as an honourable title for those who belong to God, such as Moses and the prophets. That honorific sense is present here, but it works through the image of belonging wholly to a master, not instead of it.

notes.traditional: things which must shortly be done
notes.note: The phrase can mean ‘soon’ or ‘swiftly’, that is, without delay once it begins. Most translations take it as ‘soon’, as here. The related adverb in verses 7, 12 and 20 (‘I am coming soon’) has the same ambiguity, and the King James Version has ‘quickly’ there.

The angel has been speaking, but ‘I am coming’ can only be Jesus, as verses 12–16 and 20 show. The Greek does not mark the change of speaker. Either the angel delivers Jesus’s words in the first person or Jesus’s own voice breaks in; this translation marks the words as his.

Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read ‘those who do his commandments’. The two phrases look and sound alike in Greek. The earliest witnesses read ‘wash their robes’, which recalls 7:14, and nearly all modern editions follow them.

Dogs in the ancient Mediterranean world were mostly scavengers, and ‘dog’ was a common term of contempt for the unclean or the wicked. Some scholars see a specific reference to male cult prostitutes, as in Deuteronomy 23:18, but this is uncertain.

‘Church’ is the near-universal rendering, and readers know what it refers to. A first-century hearer knew the word as the term for a civic gathering and as the Septuagint’s word for Israel assembled, whereas ‘church’ now suggests a building or institution. The preposition before it is also open: the testimony may be ‘for’, ‘in’ or ‘about’ the assemblies.

The speaker of verses 18–19 is not named. Verse 20 calls Jesus ‘the one who testifies to these things’, so this translation assigns the warning to him, but many interpreters take it as John’s own closing words. The same uncertainty applies to verses 14–15, which may be John’s comment rather than a continuation of Jesus’s speech.

notes.phrase: share in the tree of life
notes.traditional: his part out of the book of life
notes.note: The King James Version reads ‘book of life’, following the first printed Greek text, which at this point depended on the Latin, where ‘book’ and ‘tree’ differ by two letters. Virtually all Greek manuscripts read ‘tree of life’.

This prayer corresponds to the Aramaic Marana tha, ‘Our Lord, come’, which Paul quotes untranslated in 1 Corinthians 16:22. It appears to have been a fixed prayer of the earliest communities. Here it is the response to Jesus’s promise.

The manuscripts differ over the book’s last words: ‘with all’, ‘with the holy ones’, ‘with all the holy ones’ and, in the text behind the King James Version, ‘with you all’. Many add ‘Amen’. The edition translated here prints the shortest form, found in Codex Alexandrinus.

candidates.reason: It recurs throughout the New Testament for both literal slaves and God’s people, and translations split between ‘slave’ and ‘servant’; readers should see one word.
It ranges from bowing before a superior to worship of God, and needs a consistent policy, especially across the Gospels and Revelation.
It denotes cultic service to God and is rendered ‘serve’ or ‘worship’ by different translations; it must be kept distinct from προσκυνέω and δουλεύω.
The πορνεία word-family recurs in vice lists across Paul, the Gospels and Revelation, and renderings vary widely (fornicators, sexually immoral, prostitutes).

candidates.rendering: forever and ever (εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων)
candidates.reason: The ‘age’ idioms recur across the whole New Testament and need one decision between ‘forever’ and a more literal ‘to the ages of the ages’.
